providers.name: Found
providers.tagline: Business banking for the self-employed, with tax estimates and bookkeeping built in
providers.pricing_summary: Free plan with no monthly fee; Found Plus is $35/mo or $315/yr and Found Pro is $80/mo or $720/yr, adding interest on balances, extra bookkeeping tools and support perks. Found is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services are provided by Lead Bank, Member FDIC
providers.monthly_fee: $0 on the free plan; Plus $35/mo or $315/yr; Pro $80/mo or $720/yr
providers.apy: None on the free plan; Found Plus pays 1.50% APY on balances up to $20,000 and Found Pro pays 2.50% APY on all balances with no cap (variable rates, per Found's pricing page). Pro also adds 1% cash back on card purchases
providers.long_description:
Found is a business banking app for self-employed people and one-person businesses, which fits a solo handyman, cleaner or single-operator contractor with 1099 income. Found says it is a financial technology company, not a bank: banking services are provided by Lead Bank, Member FDIC, and Found states that funds are FDIC-insured up to $250,000 per depositor for each account ownership category. The company, legally Indie Technologies, Inc., says it was founded in 2019 and that over 750,000 small business owners have chosen Found.

The main idea is tax handling next to the checking account. Found says it estimates your quarterly taxes and sets money aside when you get paid. Every plan includes expense categorization, receipt scanning, real-time tax estimates, up to 20 Pockets (sub-accounts), team cards with spending controls, unlimited invoicing, and contractor management with W-9 collection and 1099 e-filing. Found says contractor payments are unlimited with no per-contractor fees.

Per Found's pricing page and fee schedule, the free plan has no monthly fee and earns no interest. Found Plus ($35/mo or $315/yr) adds 1.50% APY on balances up to $20,000, transaction importing, unlimited auto-categorization rules and priority phone support. Found Pro ($80/mo or $720/yr) pays 2.50% APY on all balances, 1% cash back on card purchases, and adds a dedicated account manager, free paper checks and $10 outgoing wires instead of $15. The fee schedule lists no overdraft or minimum balance fees, and a $10 fee on accounts dormant for 12 consecutive months.

Cash is possible but limited. Found says you can deposit cash at over 79,000 retail locations, with one free cash deposit a month and $2.00 for each one after that, up to $2,000 per rolling 7 days and $4,000 per rolling 30 days. Mobile check deposits are capped at $3,000 per week for most users, with funds typically available after 4 business days.

The trade-off: Found is built around one person's finances and taxes. Its pricing page lists no payroll, loans or line of credit, and the cash and check deposit limits are low for a trade that takes a lot of cash or large checks, so a growing shop will likely need a second account.
providers.how_it_works: You open a Found account in the app or online; the free plan has no monthly fee. As payments come in, Found estimates your self-employment taxes and sets money aside, and you can split money across up to 20 Pockets. Expenses are categorized for write-offs, receipts can be scanned, invoices are unlimited, and you can pay contractors, collect W-9s and e-file 1099s from the same app. You fund the account by bank transfer, direct deposit, mobile check deposit (up to $3,000 per week for most users) or cash at retail locations (one free cash deposit a month, then $2.00 each). Upgrading to Plus or Pro adds interest on balances and extra bookkeeping and support features; outgoing wires cost $15, or $10 on Pro.

pros_detail.title: Tax estimates and set-aside
pros_detail.explanation: Found says it estimates your quarterly taxes and sets money aside when you get paid, so a 1099 operator has tax money separated before quarterly deadlines.

pros_detail.title: Banking, bookkeeping and invoicing in one app
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes expense categorization, receipt scanning, real-time tax estimates and unlimited invoicing next to the checking account, so a solo operator may not need a separate bookkeeping tool.

pros_detail.title: Free plan with no monthly fee
pros_detail.explanation: The base plan costs $0, and Found's fee schedule lists no overdraft or minimum balance fees. Plus and Pro are optional upgrades with a 30-day free trial.

pros_detail.title: Contractor payments and 1099s
pros_detail.explanation: Found says contractor payments are unlimited with no per-contractor fees, and every plan includes W-9 collection and 1099 e-filing, handy for a solo who pays helpers now and then.

pros_detail.title: Interest on paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: Found Plus pays 1.50% APY on balances up to $20,000 and Found Pro pays 2.50% APY with no cap (variable rates), so tax reserves can earn interest if the plan fee makes sense for your balance.

cons_detail.title: Built around one person's finances
cons_detail.explanation: Found is aimed at the self-employed. It offers team cards, but its pricing page lists no payroll, so a shop with employees will need other tools.

cons_detail.title: Not a bank
cons_detail.explanation: Found is a financial technology company; banking services are provided by Lead Bank, Member FDIC. Found states that FDIC insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor per ownership category and only covers the failure of an insured bank.

cons_detail.title: Low cash and check deposit limits
cons_detail.explanation: Retail cash deposits are capped at $2,000 per rolling 7 days and $4,000 per rolling 30 days and cost $2.00 each after the first free one each month; mobile check deposits are capped at $3,000 per week for most users.

cons_detail.title: Interest costs a monthly fee
cons_detail.explanation: The free plan earns no APY. Interest starts on Plus ($35/mo, on balances up to $20,000), and the uncapped 2.50% rate needs Pro ($80/mo).

cons_detail.title: No credit products listed
cons_detail.explanation: Found's pricing page lists no line of credit or loans, so contractors who want working capital next to their bank account need a separate lender.

providers.best_for: Solo and 1099 trades operators (handymen, solo cleaners, single-operator contractors) who want checking, tax estimates, bookkeeping and contractor 1099s in one app
providers.weaknesses: Built for one person's finances, with no payroll listed; not a bank (Lead Bank, Member FDIC provides banking); low cash and check deposit limits; interest only on paid plans; no credit products listed
providers.affiliate_payout_note: No confirmed affiliate program; we currently earn nothing from Found

faqs.q: Who is Found best for?
faqs.a: Solo and self-employed trades operators, such as a one-person handyman, cleaner or single-operator contractor, who have 1099 income and want banking that estimates and sets aside quarterly taxes, with bookkeeping, invoicing and contractor 1099s in the same app. Its pricing page lists no payroll or credit products, so it is not built for a growing shop with employees.

faqs.q: How much does Found cost?
faqs.a: The free plan has no monthly fee and includes checking, tax estimates, bookkeeping, invoicing and contractor management. Found Plus is $35/mo or $315/yr and Found Pro is $80/mo or $720/yr; they add interest on balances and extra bookkeeping and support features. Other fees on Found's fee schedule include $15 outgoing wires ($10 on Pro), $1 per outgoing paper check (free on Pro) and a $10 dormancy fee after 12 months of inactivity.

faqs.q: Is Found a real bank?
faqs.a: No. Found says it is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services are provided by Lead Bank, Member FDIC. Found states that funds are FDIC-insured up to $250,000 per depositor for each account ownership category, and that FDIC insurance only covers the failure of an FDIC-insured bank.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash with Found?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. Found says account holders can deposit cash at over 79,000 retail locations. The first cash deposit each month is free and each one after that costs $2.00; deposits must be at least $5 and are capped at $2,000 per rolling 7 days and $4,000 per rolling 30 days. A trade that banks a lot of cash will likely need a second account.

faqs.q: Does Found pay interest?
faqs.a: Only on paid plans. Per Found's pricing page, Found Plus pays 1.50% APY on balances up to $20,000 and Found Pro pays 2.50% APY on all balances with no cap; the free plan earns no interest. Found says the APY is variable and subject to change.

providers.name: Novo
providers.tagline: No-monthly-fee small-business checking with invoicing and built-in savings buckets
providers.pricing_summary: No monthly fee, no minimum balance and a $0.00 insufficient funds charge per Novo's fee schedule; incoming wires and ACH are free, outgoing domestic wires cost up to $45, and third-party ATM fees are reimbursed up to $7 a month. Novo is a fintech, not a bank; banking services are provided by Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A., Member FDIC
providers.apy: 0% APY on checking per Novo's fee schedule; Reserves buckets are for setting money aside, not for earning interest
providers.long_description:
Novo is a no-monthly-fee business checking account for small and independent businesses, run by Novo Platform Inc. Novo says it is a fintech, not a bank: banking services are provided by Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A., Member FDIC, and deposits are insured up to $250,000 through that partner bank. Novo's homepage says it is trusted by 250,000+ independent businesses.

Per Novo's fee schedule (last revised February 26, 2026), the account has no monthly service charge, a $0 minimum balance, and $0 fees for insufficient funds, stop payments, incoming ACH and incoming domestic or foreign wires. Outgoing domestic wires cost up to $45, express ACH delivery costs 1.5% (minimum $0.50, maximum $20), and express check deposit costs up to 2% of the check. Novo does not charge ATM fees and reimburses third-party ATM fees up to $7 a month. Checking earns 0% APY.

For a small trades operator, the useful parts are built-in invoicing with tracking of when invoices are viewed and paid, and Novo Reserves, which lets you create up to 20 separate buckets inside the checking account for taxes, payroll or slow seasons. Novo names integrations with Stripe, QuickBooks, Shopify, Square and Xero, among what it says are over 40 business tools. It also offers a business credit card with no annual fee and up to 2% cash back (1% if your checking balance is under $5,000) and business loans, both issued by Continental Bank, plus a merchant cash advance from Novo Funding LLC.

The trade-off: Novo says it does not accept cash deposits at branches or ATMs. Its suggested workarounds are buying a money order and mobile-depositing it, or keeping a local bank account for cash and moving the money over by ACH. A trade that takes a lot of cash, or wants interest on its balance, will need a second account.
providers.how_it_works: You open a Novo business checking account online; there is no monthly fee or minimum balance. You get a debit card issued by Middlesex Federal Savings, send invoices from the account and track when they are viewed and paid, and split money into up to 20 Reserves buckets for taxes, payroll or materials. Money comes in by ACH, wire, FedNow or mobile check deposit; Novo does not accept cash, so it suggests converting cash to a money order or running it through a local bank. Third-party ATM fees are reimbursed up to $7 a month, and outgoing domestic wires cost up to $45. Eligible customers can apply for Novo's business credit card, business loans or a merchant cash advance.

pros_detail.title: No monthly fee and few fees
pros_detail.explanation: Novo's fee schedule lists no monthly service charge, a $0 minimum balance, and $0 for insufficient funds, stop payments, incoming wires and card replacement, so the everyday cost of the account is low.

pros_detail.title: Built-in invoicing
pros_detail.explanation: You can create and send invoices from the account and see when they are viewed and paid, so a one- or two-person shop can bill customers without a separate tool.

pros_detail.title: Reserves buckets
pros_detail.explanation: Novo Reserves lets you create up to 20 separate buckets inside the checking account for taxes, payroll, slow seasons or materials, a simple way to keep money set aside.

pros_detail.title: Software integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Novo names integrations with Stripe, QuickBooks, Shopify, Square and Xero and says it connects to over 40 business tools.

pros_detail.title: Credit options alongside checking
pros_detail.explanation: Eligible customers can get a no-annual-fee business credit card (up to 2% cash back with a $5,000+ checking balance) and business loans, both issued by Continental Bank, plus a merchant cash advance.

cons_detail.title: No cash deposits
cons_detail.explanation: Novo says it does not accept cash deposits at branches or ATMs. The workarounds it suggests, money orders or a separate local bank account, add cost and steps for a trade that takes cash.

cons_detail.title: No interest on checking
cons_detail.explanation: Novo's fee schedule lists a 0% APY, so idle balances and Reserves buckets do not earn interest.

cons_detail.title: Outgoing wires and fast transfers cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Outgoing domestic wires cost up to $45, express ACH is 1.5% (up to $20), and express check deposit is up to 2% of the check.

cons_detail.title: ATM reimbursement is capped
cons_detail.explanation: Third-party ATM fees are reimbursed only up to $7 a month, which a crew that pulls cash often can exceed.

cons_detail.title: Fintech, not a bank
cons_detail.explanation: Novo is a fintech; banking services are provided by Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A., Member FDIC, and deposits are insured up to $250,000 through that bank.

providers.best_for: Small, card-and-digital trades businesses that want no-monthly-fee checking with invoicing, savings buckets and software integrations, and that handle little cash
providers.weaknesses: No cash deposits (Novo suggests money orders or a second bank); 0% APY; outgoing domestic wires up to $45; ATM reimbursement capped at $7 a month; fintech (Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A. provides banking)
providers.affiliate_payout_note: No confirmed affiliate program; we currently earn nothing from Novo

faqs.q: How much does Novo cost?
faqs.a: Novo's fee schedule lists no monthly service charge and a $0 minimum balance, with $0 fees for insufficient funds, stop payments, incoming ACH and incoming wires. Fees that do apply include up to $45 for an outgoing domestic wire, 1.5% for express ACH (minimum $0.50, maximum $20) and up to 2% for express check deposit. Third-party ATM fees are reimbursed up to $7 a month.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash with Novo?
faqs.a: No. Novo says it does not accept cash deposits at branches or ATMs. It suggests buying a money order with the cash and mobile-depositing it, or keeping a local bank account for cash and moving the balance to Novo by ACH. If cash is a big part of your business, Novo should not be your only account.

faqs.q: Is Novo good for contractors?
faqs.a: It suits small trades businesses that are paid mostly by card, ACH or check and want no-monthly-fee checking, invoicing, Reserves buckets and integrations with tools like QuickBooks and Stripe. It is a weaker fit for cash-heavy shops or anyone who wants interest on their balance.

faqs.q: Does Novo pay interest?
faqs.a: No. Novo's fee schedule lists a 0% APY on the checking account. Reserves lets you set money aside in up to 20 buckets, but those buckets do not earn interest.

faqs.q: Is Novo a real bank?
faqs.a: No. Novo Platform Inc. says it is a fintech, not a bank. Banking services are provided by Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A., Member FDIC, and Novo says deposits are insured up to $250,000 through that partner bank.

providers.name: Relay
providers.tagline: Multi-account business banking built around Profit First cash management
providers.pricing_summary: Starter is free (1.19% savings APY); Grow is $30/mo (1.87% APY); Scale is $90/mo for a limited time, down from $120 (3.21% APY), with APYs as of September 17, 2026. Up to 20 checking accounts per business (50 on Scale) plus up to two savings accounts; no overdraft or NSF fees; domestic wires $8 on Starter and $5 on paid plans. Banking services provided by Thread Bank, Member FDIC, with up to $3M FDIC coverage through its sweep program
providers.apy: Savings APY of 1.19% (Starter), 1.87% (Grow) or 3.21% (Scale) as of September 17, 2026, per Relay; rates are variable
providers.long_description:
Relay is a business banking platform built for cash management, especially the Profit First method, where each deposit is split right away into separate accounts for profit, owner pay, taxes and operating costs. Relay Financial Technologies Inc. is based in Toronto; Relay says banking services are provided by Thread Bank, Member FDIC. In May 2026 Relay said it served over 150,000 small businesses and held $1.3 billion in customer deposits, after a $50 million investment from General Catalyst.

The core feature is many accounts under one login: up to 20 checking accounts (50 on Scale) and up to two savings accounts, with auto-transfer rules that split incoming money by percentage on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule. Relay says it is the official banking platform for Profit First, endorsed by the method's creator Mike Michalowicz, and you can give a Profit First Professional a role-based login. All plans include unlimited users, debit cards (up to 50 per cardholder per checking account) and credit cards with cash back.

Pricing per Relay's pricing page and deposit agreement: Starter is free with 1.19% savings APY, Grow is $30/mo with 1.87% APY, and Scale is $90/mo for a limited time (list $120) with 3.21% APY; APYs are variable and quoted as of September 17, 2026. Relay charges no overdraft or NSF fees. Domestic wires cost $8 on Starter and $5 on Grow and Scale, and same-day ACH costs $1, $0.50 or nothing depending on plan. Relay says deposits get up to $3 million of FDIC coverage when Thread Bank places them at program banks, up to $250,000 per bank. Cash can go in through Green Dot at participating retailers (up to $1,500 a day and $5,000 a month) or at Allpoint ATMs (up to $2,000 a day). Relay Capital term loans are available through Fundbox and its bank partner, Lead Bank.

The trade-off: the multi-account system only pays off if you set up and keep up the allocations, the higher savings rates need a paid plan, and cash deposits have daily and monthly caps. Relay's partner bank, Thread Bank, also agreed to an FDIC consent order in May 2024 covering anti-money-laundering controls and oversight of its fintech partners, so it makes sense to keep a backup account.
providers.how_it_works: You open a Relay account (banking services provided by Thread Bank, Member FDIC) and create up to 20 checking accounts (50 on Scale) and up to two savings accounts under one login, each for a job such as taxes, materials, owner pay or profit. Auto-transfer rules split each deposit by percentage on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule, the Profit First approach. You can add unlimited users with role-based access, issue debit cards with spending controls, and pay bills and send invoices from the same dashboard. Cash goes in through Green Dot retailers or Allpoint ATMs within Relay's limits. Savings earn 1.19%, 1.87% or 3.21% APY depending on plan (Starter free, Grow $30/mo, Scale $90/mo discounted from $120), and Thread Bank's sweep program extends FDIC coverage up to $3 million.

pros_detail.title: Multi-account Profit First structure
pros_detail.explanation: Up to 20 checking accounts (50 on Scale) and up to two savings accounts under one login, with auto-transfer rules, let you split every deposit into tax, owner-pay, materials and profit buckets automatically.

pros_detail.title: Free Starter plan
pros_detail.explanation: Starter costs $0 a month and still includes the multi-account setup, unlimited users and 1.19% APY on savings, and Relay's fee schedule lists no overdraft or NSF fees.

pros_detail.title: Savings APY rises with plan
pros_detail.explanation: Savings earn 1.19% APY on Starter, 1.87% on Grow and 3.21% on Scale (variable, as of September 17, 2026), so tax and materials reserves can earn interest.

pros_detail.title: Cards and users for a crew
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes unlimited users, up to 50 debit cards per cardholder per checking account with spending controls, and credit cards with 1%-1.5% cash back depending on plan.

pros_detail.title: FDIC coverage up to $3 million
pros_detail.explanation: Relay says deposits qualify for up to $3,000,000 of FDIC coverage when Thread Bank places them at program banks, up to $250,000 per bank, which helps a contractor holding large reserves.

cons_detail.title: Partner bank under a 2024 FDIC order
cons_detail.explanation: Thread Bank, Relay's partner bank, agreed to an FDIC consent order dated May 21, 2024 that required fixes to its anti-money-laundering program, oversight of fintech partners and liquidity management. Keep a backup account.

cons_detail.title: Cash deposits are capped
cons_detail.explanation: Cash goes in through Green Dot retailers (up to $1,500 a day, $3,500 a week and $5,000 a month, and Green Dot may charge a fee) or Allpoint ATMs (up to $2,000 a day), which can be tight for a cash-heavy trade.

cons_detail.title: Top savings rate needs a paid plan
cons_detail.explanation: The 1.87% and 3.21% APYs require Grow ($30/mo) or Scale ($90/mo on a limited-time discount from $120).

cons_detail.title: Wires and same-day ACH cost extra on lower plans
cons_detail.explanation: Domestic wires cost $8 on Starter and $5 on Grow and Scale, and same-day ACH costs $1 on Starter and $0.50 on Grow.

cons_detail.title: The system takes discipline
cons_detail.explanation: Relay's value comes from setting up and maintaining the allocations. If you will not keep the buckets current, a single simple account may serve you just as well.

providers.best_for: Contractors who want disciplined cash management, splitting every deposit into tax, materials, owner-pay and profit accounts (Profit First), with multi-user access and crew debit cards
providers.weaknesses: Partner Thread Bank agreed to an FDIC consent order in May 2024; cash deposits are capped; higher savings APY requires a paid plan; wire fees on every plan; the multi-account system needs discipline to pay off
providers.affiliate_payout_note: No confirmed affiliate program; we currently earn nothing from Relay

faqs.q: What makes Relay different from other business banking?
faqs.a: Relay is built for cash management: you can open up to 20 checking accounts (50 on Scale) and up to two savings accounts under one login and set auto-transfer rules that split every deposit by percentage. That multi-account structure, plus unlimited users and debit cards with spending controls, is its main difference from a single-account setup.

faqs.q: How much does Relay cost?
faqs.a: Starter is free and earns 1.19% APY on savings. Grow is $30/mo (1.87% APY) and Scale is $90/mo on a limited-time discount from $120 (3.21% APY); APYs are variable and quoted as of September 17, 2026. Relay charges no overdraft or NSF fees, but domestic wires cost $8 on Starter and $5 on paid plans.

faqs.q: Is Relay safe given the Thread Bank consent order?
faqs.a: Relay says banking services are provided by Thread Bank, Member FDIC, and that deposits qualify for up to $3 million of FDIC coverage through Thread Bank's sweep program. Thread Bank agreed to an FDIC consent order dated May 21, 2024 that required it to strengthen its anti-money-laundering program, fintech-partner oversight and liquidity management. FDIC insurance protects deposits if an insured bank fails; it is still prudent to keep a backup account.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash with Relay?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. Relay's deposit agreement allows cash deposits through the Green Dot network at participating retailers (generally up to $500 per deposit, $1,000 at Walmart, $1,500 a day and $5,000 a month, and Green Dot may charge its own fee) and at Allpoint ATMs (up to $1,000 per deposit and $2,000 a day). A trade that banks a lot of cash may still need a local bank.

faqs.q: Is Relay good for the Profit First method?
faqs.a: It is built for it. Relay says it is the official banking platform for Profit First, endorsed by the method's creator Mike Michalowicz. Its separate accounts and auto-transfer rules let you allocate each deposit into profit, owner-pay, tax and operating buckets, and you can give a Profit First Professional a role-based login.

providers.name: Bluevine
providers.tagline: Business checking that pays interest, plus lines of credit up to $250,000
providers.pricing_summary: Standard checking has no monthly fee and earns 1.3% APY on up to $250,000 in months you meet an activity requirement; Plus ($30/mo) earns 1.75% on up to $250,000 and Premier ($95/mo) earns 3.0% on all balances, with each fee waived if you meet balance and card-spend minimums. Lines of credit from $1,000 to $250,000 are issued by Celtic Bank. Banking services are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Valley National Bancorp agreed in September 2026 to acquire Bluevine
providers.monthly_fee: $0 Standard; Plus $30/mo and Premier $95/mo, each waived with balance and card-spend minimums
providers.apy: Standard 1.3% APY on balances up to $250,000 in months you spend $500 on the debit card or receive $2,500 in client payments; Plus 1.75% on balances up to $250,000; Premier 3.0% on all balances (per Bluevine's help center)
providers.long_description:
Bluevine pairs interest-paying business checking with lines of credit. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey, it serves about 175,000 active small business customers, according to a September 28, 2026 announcement that Valley National Bancorp will acquire Bluevine for about $340 million. The deal is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, so account terms and partner banks could change after that. For now, Bluevine says banking services are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC, with FDIC insurance up to $3,000,000 per depositor through Coastal and its program banks.

There are three checking plans, per Bluevine's help center. Standard has no monthly fee and earns 1.3% APY on balances up to $250,000 in any month you spend $500 with the Bluevine debit card or receive $2,500 in client payments. Plus costs $30/mo and earns 1.75% on balances up to $250,000; the fee is waived with a $20,000 average daily balance and $2,000 in Bluevine card spend. Premier costs $95/mo and earns 3.0% on all balances; the fee is waived with a $100,000 average daily balance and $5,000 in card spend. You can open up to 50 sub-accounts depending on plan, each with its own account number.

The Bluevine Line of Credit runs from $1,000 to $250,000, is issued by Celtic Bank and serviced by Bluevine, and is repaid weekly over up to 52 weeks or monthly over 12 months. To qualify, Bluevine asks for at least 12 months in business, $10,000 in monthly revenue, a personal FICO score of 625 or higher, and an LLC or corporation; sole proprietors and businesses in Nevada, North Dakota and South Dakota are not eligible.

Fees are low but not zero. Overdraft, NSF, incoming wire, standard ACH and mobile check deposit fees are $0, and MoneyPass ATMs are free. Standard charges $15 for an outgoing domestic wire, $10 for same-day ACH, $2.50 at out-of-network ATMs and $1.50 per printed check payment; Plus and Premier discount most of these. Cash can be deposited at Allpoint+ ATMs for $1 plus 0.5% of the deposit, or at Green Dot retailers for up to $4.95 per deposit.

The trade-off: the interest rates are attractive, but Standard only pays in months you meet the activity test, the higher rates need either a monthly fee or large balances, cash deposits cost money, and the pending sale to Valley means some terms may change in 2027.
providers.how_it_works: You open a Bluevine business checking account online; banking services are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Standard has no monthly fee and pays 1.3% APY in months you spend $500 on the debit card or receive $2,500 in client payments; Plus ($30/mo) and Premier ($95/mo) pay 1.75% and 3.0% and waive their fees if you meet balance and card-spend minimums. You can split money into up to 50 sub-accounts, pay bills, send wires and ACH, deposit checks by phone, and deposit cash at Allpoint+ ATMs or Green Dot retailers for a fee. Separately, an LLC or corporation with at least 12 months in business can apply for a line of credit of $1,000-$250,000, issued by Celtic Bank, and repay each draw weekly or monthly.

pros_detail.title: Interest on checking
pros_detail.explanation: Standard earns 1.3% APY on up to $250,000 in months you meet the activity test, Plus earns 1.75% on up to $250,000 and Premier earns 3.0% on all balances, so tax and materials reserves can earn interest.

pros_detail.title: Line of credit up to $250,000
pros_detail.explanation: The Bluevine Line of Credit runs from $1,000 to $250,000 (issued by Celtic Bank) with weekly or monthly repayment, so a contractor can bridge payroll or materials without a separate lender.

pros_detail.title: No-fee Standard plan
pros_detail.explanation: Standard has no monthly fee, and overdraft, NSF, incoming wire, standard ACH, mobile check deposit and MoneyPass ATM fees are all $0.

pros_detail.title: Sub-accounts with their own numbers
pros_detail.explanation: Depending on plan you can open up to 50 sub-accounts, each with its own account number and earning the plan's APY on eligible balances, useful for separating tax or job money.

pros_detail.title: Fee waivers on higher plans
pros_detail.explanation: Plus is free with a $20,000 average daily balance and $2,000 card spend, and Premier with $100,000 and $5,000, so a shop that keeps larger balances can get the higher rates without the monthly fee.

cons_detail.title: Pending acquisition
cons_detail.explanation: Valley National Bancorp agreed in September 2026 to buy Bluevine, with closing expected in early 2027. Plans, rates, partner banks and the app could change after the deal closes.

cons_detail.title: Standard APY has conditions
cons_detail.explanation: Standard only pays 1.3% in months you spend $500 on the Bluevine debit card or receive $2,500 in client payments, and only on balances up to $250,000.

cons_detail.title: Top APY costs a fee or a big balance
cons_detail.explanation: 1.75% needs Plus ($30/mo) and 3.0% needs Premier ($95/mo) unless you keep a $20,000 or $100,000 average daily balance and meet card-spend minimums.

cons_detail.title: Cash deposits cost money
cons_detail.explanation: Cash goes in at Allpoint+ ATMs for $1 plus 0.5% of the deposit, or at Green Dot retailers for up to $4.95 each, which adds up for a cash-heavy trade.

cons_detail.title: Credit line has strict eligibility
cons_detail.explanation: The line of credit needs 12 months in business, $10,000 in monthly revenue, a 625+ FICO score and an LLC or corporation; sole proprietors and businesses in Nevada, North Dakota and South Dakota cannot apply.

providers.best_for: Established trades businesses (LLCs or corporations) that want to earn interest on reserves and have a line of credit available alongside checking, and that take little cash
providers.weaknesses: Pending acquisition by Valley National Bancorp (closing expected early 2027); Standard APY requires monthly activity; top APY needs a fee or large balance; cash deposits carry fees; line of credit excludes sole proprietors and some states
providers.affiliate_payout_note: No confirmed affiliate program; we currently earn nothing from Bluevine

faqs.q: How much APY does Bluevine pay?
faqs.a: Per Bluevine's help center, Standard (no monthly fee) earns 1.3% APY on balances up to $250,000 in months you spend $500 on the debit card or receive $2,500 in client payments. Plus ($30/mo) earns 1.75% on balances up to $250,000, and Premier ($95/mo) earns 3.0% on all balances. The Plus fee is waived with a $20,000 average daily balance and $2,000 in card spend; the Premier fee with $100,000 and $5,000.

faqs.q: Does Bluevine offer a line of credit?
faqs.a: Yes. The Bluevine Line of Credit ranges from $1,000 to $250,000, is issued by Celtic Bank and serviced by Bluevine, and each draw is repaid weekly over up to 52 weeks or monthly over 12 months. Bluevine asks for at least 12 months in business, $10,000 in monthly revenue, a personal FICO score of 625 or higher, and an LLC or corporation.

faqs.q: Is Bluevine being acquired?
faqs.a: Yes. On September 28, 2026 Valley National Bancorp announced an agreement to acquire Bluevine for about $340 million, with closing expected in early 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. The deal had not closed as of September 30, 2026; after closing, account terms and the bank holding deposits may change, so watch for notices from Bluevine.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash with Bluevine?
faqs.a: Yes, for a fee. Bluevine's fee list shows cash deposits at Allpoint+ ATMs cost $1 plus 0.5% of the deposit, and deposits at Green Dot retailers cost up to $4.95 each. A trade that handles a lot of cash may find a local bank cheaper for that part of the business.

faqs.q: Is my money safe with Bluevine?
faqs.a: Bluevine says banking services are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC, and that deposits are FDIC insured up to $3,000,000 per depositor through Coastal Community Bank and its program banks. FDIC insurance protects deposits if an insured bank fails.

providers.name: Mercury
providers.tagline: Online business banking with no monthly fee and up to $5M FDIC coverage via sweep, but no cash deposits
providers.pricing_summary: Mercury (free plan) $0/mo: Mercury says there are no minimum balance requirements, overdraft fees, required monthly fees or account opening fees. ACH and domestic wires are free to send and receive; international USD wires are free, or a flat $15 if you choose to cover the fees (OUR); non-USD wires carry a 1% conversion fee. QuickBooks and Xero enriched automations are free on every plan. Paid plans: Mercury Plus $29.90/mo (recurring invoices, ACH-debit invoicing at $1 per transaction) and Mercury Pro $299/mo (ACH-debit invoicing at $0, relationship manager), both lower when billed annually; enriched NetSuite automations need a paid plan.
providers.apy: No APY shown for business checking or savings; Mercury Treasury (money-market funds, not FDIC-insured) requires $250,000+ in Mercury balances
providers.long_description:
Mercury is online business banking from Mercury Technologies, a San Francisco fintech founded in 2017 that says more than 300,000 entrepreneurs use it. The free plan has no monthly fee, no minimum balance and no overdraft fees, and includes checking and savings accounts, debit cards, free ACH and domestic wires, free international USD wires, bill pay, basic invoicing and free QuickBooks and Xero automations. Mercury says deposits are FDIC-insured up to $5M through its partner banks' sweep networks, which spread money across up to 20 banks, well above the standard $250,000 per bank.

Mercury is a fintech, not a bank. Banking services are provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC. In April 2026 the OCC gave Mercury conditional approval to form its own national bank, Mercury Bank, N.A., to be headquartered in Utah; it still needs final OCC approval plus FDIC and Federal Reserve approvals, and Mercury said accounts stay with its partner banks in the meantime.

The biggest limit for trades is cash: Mercury's FAQ says it does not support cash deposits, and the partner bank's deposit agreement says it does not accept cash. You fund the account by ACH, wire or remote check deposit through the dashboard. There are no branches, and Mercury says customers must be formed and registered in the United States or a US territory.

The trade-off: Mercury gives an electronically paid contractor free banking, free wires, accounting sync and large FDIC coverage, but a business that collects cash needs a second account somewhere that takes it.
providers.how_it_works: Apply online; there are no branches. Mercury says customers must be formed and registered in the United States or a US territory. Deposits are held at partner banks (Choice Financial Group and Column N.A.) and swept across up to 20 banks for up to $5M in FDIC coverage. Fund the account by ACH, incoming wire or remote check deposit in the dashboard; cash deposits are not supported. From one dashboard you manage debit cards, ACH and wires, bill pay, invoicing, multiple accounts and auto-transfer rules, with QuickBooks and Xero automations included on the free plan.

pros_detail.title: No monthly fee or minimum
pros_detail.explanation: Mercury says its business banking has no minimum balance requirements, overdraft fees, required monthly fees or account opening fees.

pros_detail.title: Up to $5M FDIC via sweep
pros_detail.explanation: Mercury says partner-bank sweep networks spread deposits across up to 20 banks for up to $5M in FDIC coverage, useful when a large project deposit lands.

pros_detail.title: Free wires and ACH
pros_detail.explanation: ACH and domestic wires are free to send and receive, and international USD wires are free unless you choose to cover the fees ($15 flat).

pros_detail.title: Auto-transfer rules
pros_detail.explanation: Mercury offers scheduled payments and auto-transfer rules, so you can move money into separate accounts for taxes or upcoming jobs automatically.

pros_detail.title: Free accounting sync
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks and Xero enriched automations are free on every plan; bank-feed import to NetSuite is free, with enriched NetSuite automations on a paid plan.

cons_detail.title: No cash deposits
cons_detail.explanation: Mercury's FAQ says it does not support cash deposits, a dealbreaker for a contractor who collects cash.

cons_detail.title: No branches
cons_detail.explanation: It is online-only, so there is no teller or in-person help when something goes wrong.

cons_detail.title: A fintech, not a bank (for now)
cons_detail.explanation: Mercury itself is not an FDIC-insured bank; its own national bank has only conditional OCC approval and still needs final OCC, FDIC and Federal Reserve approvals.

cons_detail.title: Account holds and closures possible
cons_detail.explanation: The partner bank's deposit agreement lets it freeze or hold funds while it investigates suspected irregular activity and close an account at any time.

cons_detail.title: Some features cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Recurring and ACH-debit invoicing need Plus ($29.90/mo) or Pro ($299/mo), and non-USD wires carry a 1% conversion fee.

providers.best_for: US-registered contractors and agencies paid by ACH, check, wire or card (not cash) who want online banking with no monthly fee and large FDIC coverage
providers.weaknesses: No cash deposits; no branches; a fintech relying on partner banks while its own bank charter awaits final approval; partner-bank terms allow holds, freezes and closures; recurring and ACH-debit invoicing need a paid plan
providers.reputation_flag: Mercury's BBB profile lists 151 complaints closed in the last three years, and Mercury is not BBB accredited. Its partner bank's deposit agreement allows freezes and holds during investigations and account closure at any time, so keep a backup account.
providers.affiliate_program: Yes: referral program ($250 each when a referred business deposits $10K in 90 days); advisor program up to $1,500/client
providers.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD until the tracking link is confirmed

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash with Mercury?
faqs.a: No. Mercury's FAQ says it does not currently support cash deposits, and its partner bank's deposit agreement says it does not accept cash. You can fund the account by ACH, wire or remote check deposit. If your business collects meaningful cash, pair Mercury with a bank that takes cash deposits or choose a different account.

faqs.q: Is Mercury a real bank, and is my money safe?
faqs.a: Mercury is a fintech, not a bank. Banking services are provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC, and Mercury says their sweep networks give up to $5M in FDIC coverage across up to 20 banks. In April 2026 Mercury received conditional OCC approval to form Mercury Bank, N.A., but it still needs final OCC, FDIC and Federal Reserve approvals. FDIC insurance covers bank failure, not an account hold or closure.

faqs.q: Is Mercury free?
faqs.a: The base Mercury plan is $0/mo with no minimum balance, overdraft fees or opening fees, and it includes free ACH, domestic wires and international USD wires plus free QuickBooks and Xero automations. Mercury Plus ($29.90/mo) adds recurring invoices and ACH-debit invoicing at $1 per transaction; Mercury Pro ($299/mo) makes ACH-debit invoicing free and adds a relationship manager. Non-USD wires carry a 1% conversion fee.

faqs.q: Is Mercury good for contractors?
faqs.a: It fits US-registered contractors and agencies that get paid electronically and want online banking with no monthly fee, strong FDIC coverage and accounting sync. It does not fit trades that deposit cash or want a branch to walk into. Match it to how you actually get paid.

providers.name: Lili
providers.tagline: Online business banking with tax set-aside and bookkeeping on paid plans, plus retail cash deposits
providers.pricing_summary: Lili Core $0/mo with no minimum balance. Lili Pro $15/mo ($9/mo for the first 3 months) adds automatic tax-savings allocation, expense tax categories and expense reports. Lili Smart $35/mo ($21/mo for 3 months) adds unlimited invoicing, bill pay, AI bookkeeping and P&L and cash-flow reports. Lili Premium $55/mo ($33/mo for 3 months) adds a metal debit card and a dedicated specialist. Outgoing wires $15 domestic, $25 international. Savings APY is variable: 2.25% on balances up to $500,000 and 4.00% on balances over $500,000 up to $1,000,000; no interest above $1M. FDIC coverage up to $3M through Sunrise Banks, N.A. and its sweep network banks. BusinessBuild credit-building add-on $18/mo for 3 months, then $30/mo.
providers.apy: 2.25% APY (variable) on savings balances up to $500,000; 4.00% on balances over $500,000 up to $1,000,000; no interest above $1M
providers.long_description:
Lili is an online business banking platform for small business owners, based in New York; banking services are provided by Sunrise Banks, N.A., Member FDIC. Lili says it serves more than 200,000 businesses and supports sole proprietors, single- and multi-member LLCs, partnerships and corporations. The free Core plan includes business checking with a Visa debit card, ACH, check and wire payments, fee-free withdrawals at MoneyPass ATMs, a high-yield savings account and up to $3M in FDIC coverage through a sweep network.

The tax and bookkeeping tools are what set Lili apart for a one-person trade, but they are on paid plans. Pro ($15/mo) lets you preset a percentage of each payment to move into a tax bucket automatically and sorts expenses into tax categories with quarterly and yearly reports. Smart ($35/mo) adds unlimited invoicing with card acceptance, bill pay, AI transaction categorization, P&L and cash-flow reports, and pre-filled tax forms such as Schedule C. Premium ($55/mo) adds a metal card and a dedicated specialist.

Lili takes cash: you can deposit at participating retailers through Green Dot. Lili's homepage lists a limit of $1,000 per cardholder per 24 hours and a retailer fee of up to $4.95, and some locations set lower limits. Lili says it offers live support seven days a week and, since January 2026, markets team access to multi-employee businesses, saying it suits teams of up to 10.

The trade-off: the Core plan has no monthly fee, but the tax and invoicing tools cost $15-$55 a month, cash deposits are small and carry a retailer fee, there are no branches, and Lili's account agreement lets it close an account for any reason.
providers.how_it_works: Apply online with no minimum balance; banking is provided by Sunrise Banks, N.A. Money comes in by ACH, wire, mobile check deposit or cash at participating retailers through Green Dot (up to $1,000 per 24 hours, retailer fee up to $4.95). On Pro and higher plans you preset a percentage of each payment to move into a tax bucket automatically; Smart and Premium add invoicing, bill pay, bookkeeping and pre-filled tax forms. Withdraw cash fee-free at MoneyPass ATMs and connect tools such as QuickBooks, Xero, Gusto, Stripe, Square and Shopify.

pros_detail.title: Automatic tax set-aside
pros_detail.explanation: From the Pro plan ($15/mo) up, Lili moves a percentage you choose from each payment into a tax bucket, so quarterly taxes are already set aside.

pros_detail.title: Accepts cash deposits
pros_detail.explanation: You can deposit cash at participating retailers through Green Dot.

pros_detail.title: Free Core tier, no minimum
pros_detail.explanation: Core is $0/mo with no minimum balance and includes checking, a debit card, savings and fee-free MoneyPass ATM withdrawals.

pros_detail.title: High-yield savings, $3M FDIC
pros_detail.explanation: Savings pays a variable 2.25% APY up to $500,000 (4.00% only on balances above that, up to $1M), with up to $3M FDIC coverage via sweep.

pros_detail.title: Invoicing and bookkeeping in one app
pros_detail.explanation: Smart ($35/mo) adds unlimited invoicing, bill pay, P&L and cash-flow reports and pre-filled tax forms such as Schedule C.

cons_detail.title: Small cash limits plus a fee
cons_detail.explanation: Retail cash deposits are capped at $1,000 per 24 hours (lower at some locations) and retailers may charge up to $4.95 each time, so it does not suit cash-heavy shops.

cons_detail.title: Tax and accounting tools cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Core has no tax set-aside, invoicing or bookkeeping; those start at $15/mo (Pro) and $35/mo (Smart).

cons_detail.title: Wire fees
cons_detail.explanation: Outgoing wires cost $15 domestic and $25 international.

cons_detail.title: No branches
cons_detail.explanation: Lili is app- and web-based, with no branch to visit when something goes wrong.

cons_detail.title: Closure terms
cons_detail.explanation: Lili's account agreement says it may close an account for any reason, with or without notice.

providers.best_for: Solo and small trades businesses (sole proprietors and LLCs) that want banking with automatic tax set-aside and invoicing in one app and deposit only occasional cash
providers.weaknesses: Cash deposits capped at $1,000 per 24 hours with retailer fees up to $4.95; tax set-aside, invoicing and bookkeeping need a $15-$55/mo plan; $15/$25 outgoing wire fees; no branches; account agreement allows closure for any reason
providers.reputation_flag: Lili's BBB profile lists 150 complaints closed in the last three years. Its account agreement says Lili may close an account for any reason, with or without notice, so keep a backup account.
providers.affiliate_program: Refer-a-friend (reported ~$100 per qualified referral); no confirmed publisher affiliate program (verify directly)
providers.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD; referral terms unconfirmed on an owned page

faqs.q: How does Lili help with taxes?
faqs.a: On the Pro plan ($15/mo) and higher, you preset a percentage of each payment and Lili moves it into a tax bucket automatically; Pro also sorts expenses into tax categories and produces quarterly and yearly expense reports. Smart and Premium add pre-filled tax forms such as Schedule C. The free Core plan does not include these tax tools.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash into Lili?
faqs.a: Yes. Lili accepts cash deposits at participating retailers through Green Dot. Its homepage lists a limit of up to $1,000 per cardholder per 24 hours, lower at some locations, and retailer fees of up to $4.95. That works for occasional cash, not for a cash-heavy operation.

faqs.q: Is Lili free?
faqs.a: The Core plan is $0/mo with no minimum balance and includes checking, a debit card and savings. Pro ($15/mo), Smart ($35/mo) and Premium ($55/mo) are discounted to $9, $21 and $33 for the first 3 months and add tax set-aside, invoicing, bill pay and bookkeeping. Outgoing wires cost $15 domestic and $25 international.

faqs.q: Does Lili work for a business with employees?
faqs.a: Lili says it supports sole proprietors, LLCs, partnerships and corporations, offers access for team members and accountants, and suits teams of up to 10. It does not run payroll itself but connects with Gusto. A larger crew that needs branches or large cash deposits should look at a traditional bank.

providers.name: Chase Business Complete Banking
providers.tagline: Big-bank business checking with branches, free ATM cash deposits and built-in card acceptance
providers.pricing_summary: $15 monthly service fee, waived in any statement period when you meet ONE of: $2,000 minimum daily ending balance; $2,000 in eligible deposits from Chase QuickAccept or other Chase Payment Solutions; $2,000 in eligible purchases on a Chase Ink or other Chase business credit card; a linked Chase Private Client, JPMorgan Classic or Private Client Checking Plus account; or Chase Military Banking. New accounts have the first two monthly fees waived. Electronic deposits, ACH, ATM transactions and debit card purchases are free; 20 banker deposits/withdrawals and paper checks per period are free, then $0.50 each. In-branch cash deposits free up to $5,000 per period, then $3.00 per $1,000; cash deposited at Chase ATMs has no fee. Outgoing domestic wires $25 online or $35 in a branch; incoming wires $15. No minimum opening deposit. Checking earns no interest. New-account bonus: $400 (with $2,000 in new money) or $500 (with $10,000), offer valid 09/15/2026-01/21/2027.
providers.monthly_fee: $15/mo (waivable by $2,000 balance, $2,000 card spend or $2,000 QuickAccept deposits); first two months waived for new accounts
providers.long_description:
Chase Business Complete Banking is the entry-level business checking account from JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., part of JPMorgan Chase & Co. of New York. It pairs everyday checking with what an online-only bank cannot offer: Chase says its business customers get access to more than 5,000 branches and more than 14,000 ATMs, and cash deposited at a Chase ATM carries no fee. The account also includes Chase QuickAccept card acceptance with same-day deposits at no additional fee, digital invoicing from Chase Business Online or the mobile app, and Zelle, with Chase business credit cards, lines of credit and loans available from the same bank.

The monthly fee is $15, waived in any statement period when you keep a $2,000 minimum daily ending balance, take $2,000 in eligible QuickAccept or other Chase Payment Solutions deposits, spend $2,000 on a Chase Ink or other Chase business card, link a qualifying Chase Private Client account, or qualify for Chase Military Banking. New accounts get the first two monthly fees waived. Twenty banker transactions and paper checks per period are free, then $0.50 each, and in-branch cash deposits are free up to $5,000 per period, then $3.00 per $1,000.

Chase can link QuickAccept and other Chase payment processing data to QuickBooks Online at no cost, and sole proprietors, corporations and single-member LLCs can open the account online with no minimum opening deposit. As of 10 October 2026 Chase advertises a $400 or $500 new-account bonus for Business Complete (valid 09/15/2026 through 01/21/2027, conditions apply).

The trade-off: branches, free ATM cash deposits and built-in card acceptance, but a $15 fee in any month you miss a waiver, per-item fees above the free allowances, no interest, and fewer bookkeeping automations than online business accounts.
providers.how_it_works: Open online or in a branch with no minimum opening deposit (sole proprietors, corporations and single-member LLCs can apply online). The $15 monthly fee is waived for the first two statement periods and then in any period you meet one waiver, such as a $2,000 minimum daily ending balance or $2,000 in QuickAccept deposits. Deposit cash at Chase ATMs with no fee or in a branch (free up to $5,000 per period). Take card payments with QuickAccept, which deposits the same day, send invoices from Chase Business Online, and sync payment processing data to QuickBooks Online.

pros_detail.title: Branches and free ATM cash deposits
pros_detail.explanation: Chase cites more than 5,000 branches and 14,000 ATMs, and cash deposited at a Chase ATM has no fee, so a cash-collecting trade can bank the day's takings easily.

pros_detail.title: Built-in card acceptance (QuickAccept)
pros_detail.explanation: Take card payments with same-day deposits at no additional fee, and $2,000 of eligible QuickAccept deposits in a period also waives the monthly fee.

pros_detail.title: Credit and loans at the same bank
pros_detail.explanation: Chase business credit cards, lines of credit and small business loans are available alongside the checking account for financing trucks and equipment.

pros_detail.title: Invoicing, Zelle and QuickBooks Online
pros_detail.explanation: Send digital invoices from Chase Business Online or the app, use Zelle, and sync payment processing data to QuickBooks Online for free.

pros_detail.title: First two months free
pros_detail.explanation: Chase waives the first two monthly service fees on new accounts, giving time to reach a waiver.

cons_detail.title: Monthly fee unless you qualify
cons_detail.explanation: $15/mo unless you keep a $2,000 daily balance, spend $2,000 on a Chase business card or take $2,000 via QuickAccept each period, a hurdle for seasonal trades.

cons_detail.title: Limited free in-branch cash
cons_detail.explanation: In-branch cash deposits are free only up to $5,000 per period, then $3.00 per $1,000 (Chase ATM cash deposits have no fee).

cons_detail.title: Per-item fees above 20
cons_detail.explanation: After 20 banker deposits, withdrawals and paper checks per period, each costs $0.50.

cons_detail.title: Wire fees
cons_detail.explanation: Outgoing domestic wires cost $25 online or $35 in a branch, and incoming wires $15.

cons_detail.title: No interest
cons_detail.explanation: Checking earns no interest, so idle balances do not earn anything.

providers.best_for: Cash-handling and card-accepting trades who want branches, free ATM cash deposits and business credit under one roof
providers.weaknesses: $15/mo unless waived; in-branch cash free only to $5,000 per period, then $3.00 per $1,000; $0.50 per banker transaction or paper check after 20; $25-$35 outgoing wire fees; no interest on checking
providers.affiliate_program: Chase Refer a Business ($100 per referred business, up to $1,000/yr), a customer referral, not a publisher affiliate program
providers.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD; this is a customer-referral, not a standard publisher affiliate

faqs.q: Is Chase good for a cash-based contractor?
faqs.a: It is one of the easier options for cash. Chase says business customers can use more than 5,000 branches and 14,000 ATMs, and cash deposited at a Chase ATM has no fee. In-branch cash deposits are free up to $5,000 per statement period, then $3.00 per $1,000, so using the ATM keeps larger cash deposits free.

faqs.q: How do I avoid the $15 monthly fee on Chase Business Complete?
faqs.a: Meet any one of these each statement period: keep a $2,000 minimum daily ending balance, take $2,000 in eligible deposits through Chase QuickAccept or other Chase Payment Solutions, spend $2,000 on a Chase Ink or other Chase business credit card, link a Chase Private Client, JPMorgan Classic or Private Client Checking Plus account, or qualify for Chase Military Banking. New accounts also get the first two monthly fees waived.

faqs.q: Does Chase Business Complete let me take card payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Chase QuickAccept lets you accept card payments with same-day deposits at no additional fee, and $2,000 or more of eligible QuickAccept deposits in a statement period also waives the monthly fee. Card processing fees still apply to each sale.

faqs.q: Is there a signup bonus?
faqs.a: Yes, as of 10 October 2026. Chase advertises $400 for a new Business Complete account funded with $2,000 in new money, or $500 with $10,000, deposited within 30 days of enrollment and kept for 60 days, plus 5 qualifying transactions within 90 days. The offer is valid 09/15/2026 to 01/21/2027 and is not open to existing Chase business checking customers. Check Chase's site for current terms before opening.

providers.name: Bank of America Business Advantage Banking
providers.tagline: Big-bank business checking with branches and Preferred Rewards benefits that grow with your balances
providers.pricing_summary: Business Advantage Fundamentals: $16/mo, not charged until your 13th statement cycle closes, then waived in any cycle with a $5,000 combined average monthly balance in eligible linked business accounts, $500 in new net qualified business debit card purchases, or Preferred Rewards for Business membership. 20 free transactions (checks paid, other debits, deposited items) per cycle, then $0.45 each; debit card transactions, electronic debits and checks deposited by mobile, ATM or Remote Deposit Online do not count. Cash deposits free up to $5,000 per cycle, then $0.30 per $100. Business Advantage Relationship: $29.95/mo, waived with a $15,000 combined average monthly balance or Preferred Rewards; 500 free transactions and $20,000 free cash per cycle. No minimum opening deposit; both accounts are non-interest-bearing. Outgoing domestic wires $30, incoming $15. New-account bonus $400-$2,500 for $5,000-$200,000 in new money, offer expires November 30, 2026.
providers.monthly_fee: $16/mo Fundamentals (no fee for the first 12 cycles, then waivable); $29.95/mo Relationship (waivable)
providers.apy: No interest on either checking account (both are non-interest-bearing)
providers.long_description:
Bank of America Business Advantage Banking is Bank of America's small business checking, offered as two accounts you can switch between: Fundamentals for lower transaction and cash needs and Relationship for higher volumes. Bank of America, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, says it has about 3,500 financial centers and 15,000 ATMs, and the business side offers credit cards, lines of credit, equipment financing, SBA loans, merchant services and payroll.

Fundamentals costs $16 a month, but Bank of America does not charge it until your 13th statement cycle closes; after that it is waived in any cycle with a $5,000 combined average monthly balance in eligible linked business accounts, $500 in new net debit card purchases, or Preferred Rewards for Business membership. It includes 20 free counted transactions per cycle (then $0.45 each, with debit card purchases, electronic debits and mobile or ATM check deposits not counted) and $5,000 of free cash deposits per cycle, then $0.30 per $100. Relationship costs $29.95 a month unless you keep a $15,000 combined average balance or are a Preferred Rewards member, and raises the allowances to 500 transactions and $20,000 in cash.

Preferred Rewards for Business is the main reason to consolidate at Bank of America. It has three tiers based on a three-month combined average daily balance: Gold at $20,000, Platinum at $50,000 and Platinum Honors at $100,000. Members get monthly fees waived on up to four checking accounts, some wire-fee waivers, and a 25%, 50% or 75% bonus on rewards from eligible Bank of America business credit cards. Business Advantage 360 online banking includes Cash Flow Monitor, bill pay, mobile check deposit, Zelle and QuickBooks integration.

The trade-off: branch service, a full product shelf and a year without the Fundamentals fee, but the fee returns if you miss a waiver, cash above $5,000 a cycle costs $0.30 per $100 on Fundamentals, neither account earns interest, and the Preferred Rewards benefits start at $20,000 in balances.
providers.how_it_works: Open Fundamentals or Relationship online or at a financial center with no minimum opening deposit, and switch between them if your needs change. On Fundamentals no monthly fee is charged until your 13th statement cycle closes; after that meet one waiver each cycle (balance, $500 in debit card purchases or Preferred Rewards). Deposit cash and checks at financial centers and ATMs, or deposit checks by mobile. Once your combined business balances average $20,000 or more over three months you can enroll in Preferred Rewards for Business. Manage everything in Business Advantage 360 with Cash Flow Monitor, bill pay, Zelle and QuickBooks integration.

pros_detail.title: Branches and cash/check deposits
pros_detail.explanation: Bank of America cites about 3,500 financial centers and 15,000 ATMs for in-person cash and check deposits.

pros_detail.title: First year without the Fundamentals fee
pros_detail.explanation: The $16 Fundamentals fee is not charged until the 13th statement cycle closes, and $500 in monthly debit card purchases waives it after that.

pros_detail.title: Preferred Rewards scales with you
pros_detail.explanation: At $20,000, $50,000 and $100,000 in combined balances, members get fee waivers on up to four checking accounts and a 25%, 50% or 75% bonus on eligible business card rewards.

pros_detail.title: Full product shelf

faqs.q: How does Bank of America Preferred Rewards help a contractor?
faqs.a: Once your qualifying business balances average $20,000 (Gold), $50,000 (Platinum) or $100,000 (Platinum Honors) over three months, you can enroll in Preferred Rewards for Business. Members get monthly fees waived on up to four Business Advantage checking accounts, a 25%, 50% or 75% bonus on rewards from eligible Bank of America business credit cards, and some wire-fee waivers at higher tiers.

faqs.q: What does Business Advantage cost and how do I avoid the fee?
faqs.a: Fundamentals is $16/mo, but Bank of America does not charge it until your 13th statement cycle closes. After that it is waived by a $5,000 combined average monthly balance in eligible linked business accounts, $500 in new net debit card purchases, or Preferred Rewards membership. Relationship is $29.95/mo, waived at a $15,000 combined average balance or through Preferred Rewards. Neither account needs a minimum deposit to open.

faqs.q: Can I deposit cash at Bank of America?
faqs.a: Yes, at financial centers and ATMs. Fundamentals includes $5,000 in free cash deposits per statement cycle, counting both ATM and financial-center deposits, then $0.30 per $100. Relationship raises the free amount to $20,000 per cycle.

faqs.q: Is there a signup bonus for Bank of America business checking?
faqs.a: Yes, as of 30 September 2026. providers.long_description:
U.S. Bank Business Essentials is a business checking account from U.S. Bank National Association, part of Minneapolis-based U.S. Bancorp, whose national bank charter dates to 1863. It has no monthly maintenance fee and no minimum balance, needs a $25 opening deposit, and includes branch access and card acceptance: U.S. Bank cites more than 2,000 branches and fee-free transactions at over 13,000 ATMs, and the account comes with payment processing and a first mobile card reader at no charge.

For a trade that takes cards in the field, the built-in processing charges 2.60% + $0.10 for tap or insert payments, 3.50% + $0.15 keyed and 2.90% + $0.30 online, with no monthly software fee. U.S. Bank advertises same-day access to card funds; its fine print says payments arrive the next day or within 24 hours of batch processing, with batches processed every day including weekends. U.S. Bank's business lending (term loans, lines of credit, SBA loans, equipment financing) is available as you grow, and business accounts can connect to QuickBooks Online.

The free allowances are modest. You get 25 teller or paper-check transactions per cycle, then $0.50 each, and 25 cash deposit units, where each unit is about $100 (any deposit under $150 counts as one), then $0.35 per $100. Sending ACH payments from online banking costs $1 each, wires cost $30 online, and paper statements cost $6.50 per cycle unless you switch to e-statements. As of 30 September 2026 U.S. Bank offers a $400 bonus for new Business Essentials accounts (promo code Q4DIG26, open by 1/13/2027).

The trade-off: a no-monthly-fee account with branches, cash deposits and built-in card acceptance, but small free cash and teller allowances, per-item fees on outgoing ACH and wires, and no interest.
providers.how_it_works: Open online or in a branch with a $25 deposit. Electronic deposits, debit card purchases, ATM transactions and mobile check deposits carry no transaction fee; teller transactions and paper checks are free up to 25 per cycle. Deposit cash at branches or U.S. Bank partner ATMs (25 cash units, roughly $2,500, free per cycle). Take card payments with the included mobile card reader or online, with funds deposited daily into the checking account, including weekends. Switch to e-statements to avoid the paper statement fee.

faqs.q: Is U.S. Bank Business Essentials really free?
faqs.a: It has a $0 monthly maintenance fee and no minimum balance, with a $25 opening deposit. Electronic deposits and withdrawals, debit card purchases and ATM transactions carry no transaction fee, and 25 teller transactions and paper checks per cycle are included. Some services cost extra: $0.50 per teller or paper item after 25, $1 to send an ACH payment from online banking, $30-$40 for outgoing wires and $6.50 per cycle for paper statements.

faqs.q: How much cash can I deposit for free?
faqs.a: 25 cash deposit units per statement cycle. U.S. Bank counts units by dividing each cash deposit by $100 and rounding, and any deposit under $150 counts as one unit, so the allowance is roughly $2,500 in larger deposits and less if you make many small ones. After that the fee is $0.35 per $100.

faqs.q: Can I take card payments with U.S. Bank Business Essentials?
faqs.a: Yes. The account includes payment processing with a first mobile card reader at no charge (extra readers $89). Tap or insert payments cost 2.60% + $0.10, keyed 3.50% + $0.15 and online 2.90% + $0.30. U.S. Bank advertises same-day access to funds; its fine print says payments arrive the next day or within 24 hours of batch processing, with batches processed every day including weekends.

faqs.q: What is the signup bonus?
faqs.a: As of 30 September 2026, U.S. Bank offers $400 for a new Business Essentials account opened between 9/28/2026 and 1/13/2027 with promo code Q4DIG26: deposit $5,000 in new money within 30 days, keep that daily balance through day 60, and make 6 qualifying transactions within 60 days.
